checks.title: New mail reaches every open mail app under one rising UID
checks.gherkin:
Scenario: New mail reaches every open mail app under one rising UID
  Given Sean's mailbox holds two messages
  And his Mac is idling on INBOX
  And his phone has INBOX selected
  When a message is delivered to his mailbox
  Then the Mac is told "* 3 EXISTS" without sending a command
  And the phone is told "* 3 EXISTS" on its next NOOP
  And both fetch message 3 under the same UID, greater than every UID before it
proves: SHALL keep each mailbox in one Durable Object that pulls deliveries into SQLite, assigning UIDs that only rise
SHALL tell every registered IMAP session of any change
toy.01a19d7e: a ping tells every IDLE session, and the mailbox object never reuses a UID
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: Receiving mail across two apps runs the receiver, the ping, the pull, the tell and both sessions end to end, which no single module holds.

checks.title: A message deleted on one device stays readable on another until it is told
checks.gherkin:
Scenario: A message deleted on one device stays readable on another until it is told
  Given Sean's Mac and phone both have INBOX selected
  And each was told that message 1 has a UID
  When he deletes message 1 on the phone with STORE +FLAGS (\Deleted) and EXPUNGE
  Then the Mac's FETCH 1 (UID BODY[]) still returns that UID and the message's bytes
  And the Mac's next NOOP tells "* 1 EXPUNGE"
  And a fresh SELECT on either device no longer lists that UID
proves: SHALL keep an expunged message's bytes readable until they are erased (FR-MAIL-053)
SHALL tell every registered IMAP session of any change
form.01a19daa idea 4: expunge hides and does not erase, so another session can still read the message it was told about
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: Deleting on one device and reading on another is a person's action across two live sessions and the mailbox, start to finish.

checks.title: A message marked read on one device shows read on another
checks.gherkin:
Scenario: A message marked read on one device shows read on another
  Given Sean's Mac is idling on INBOX
  And his phone has INBOX selected
  When he reads message 1 on the phone, which stores \Seen on it
  Then the Mac is told message 1's flags include \Seen without sending a command
proves: SHALL tell every registered IMAP session of any change
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: Marking mail read is something a person does, and its effect is seen on a second device through the whole chain.

checks.title: UIDs rise and are never reused after expunge
checks.rule: Each added message takes a UID greater than every UID the mailbox has assigned, including UIDs of expunged rows, and open reports uidNext as sqlite_sequence.seq + 1.
proves: SHALL assign UIDs that only rise
form.01a19daa claim: AUTOINCREMENT with expunged rows kept never reuses a UID
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: UID assignment is the mailbox object's own logic, and no person does anything distinct to trigger it.

checks.title: A fresh mailbox object takes a greater UID validity
checks.rule: A mailbox object whose tables are created anew sets uid_validity from the current time in seconds, greater than the value of any earlier object for the same mailbox.
proves: SHALL assign UIDs that only rise
rfc3501.2.3.1.1: a mailbox whose UIDs fail to persist must take a greater UIDVALIDITY
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: A rebuilt object is an internal event with no user action of its own.

checks.title: A delivery committing behind the newest id is pulled once
checks.rule: A delivery whose UUIDv7 id is older than the newest id already seen, by less than ten minutes, and that commits after it, is added exactly once, as is every row of a burst of more than 100 deliveries inside those ten minutes.
proves: SHALL never lose a delivery that commits late
form.01a19daa Pulling: the cursor stands ten minutes behind the newest id seen, dashed, and pages by the last id read
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: Commit order against id order is timing inside the pull; the person only receives mail, which the first scenario already covers.

checks.title: One bad delivery is skipped and later ones still pull
checks.rule: A delivery whose blob is gone, or whose read or insert fails, gets a skipped row (no-blob or unreadable) and every later delivery, in this pull and the next, is still added.
proves: SHALL never let one bad message stop later ones
form.01a19daa Pulling: skipped rows for no-blob and unreadable
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: A bad message comes from a stranger or from damage, not from anything the mailbox's owner does.

checks.title: An expunged row is still served, and its row outlives its bytes
checks.rule: held and bytes serve a row whether expunged or not, held answers for 101 UIDs within the 100-parameter limit, open never lists an expunged row, and once the blob is gone held still returns the row while bytes returns null.
proves: SHALL keep an expunged message's bytes readable until they are erased (FR-MAIL-053) and its row after that
toy.01a1a4ad must_hold: keep the tombstone, since removing the row closes a woken session with 1011
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: The person's side of this is the second scenario; the row outliving its bytes follows erasure, which no person triggers here.

checks.title: Every change tells every registered session
checks.rule: Any commit that adds, flags or expunges a row, from open, ping, setFlags, expunge or the alarm, calls changed() on every registered session; a false forgets that name, and a rejection keeps it while the others are still told.
proves: SHALL tell every registered IMAP session of any change
form.01a19daa Telling: whenever a pull adds a row, from any caller, every registered session is told
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: Which caller triggers a tell, and what a refused tell does to the registry, cannot be reached from the client side.

checks.title: Nothing waits for a tell
checks.rule: With a session whose changed() sits behind a real serial queue, open, ping, setFlags, expunge and alarm each return while a tell is outstanding, and a changed() that never settles is cut off at 10 seconds without stopping later passes.
proves: SHALL tell every registered IMAP session of any change without ever waiting for the telling
form.01a19daa provenance: a tell cycle hung a mailbox and every ping for good on local workerd
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: The hang is a cycle between a session's queue and the mailbox's calls, which only a fake session with a real queue can hold in place.

checks.title: An untold commit is told by the next alarm
checks.rule: A commit sets tell-owed in its own transaction, and alarm() first sets the next alarm while a session is registered, then pulls, then tells when tell-owed is set, so a lost tell, a lost ping or a pull that throws still ends in a tell.
proves: SHALL tell every registered IMAP session of any change
form.01a19daa Telling: a commit that has not been told must not stay untold
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: A lost tell or a D1 outage is an internal failure that no person can cause on purpose.

gaps.failure_way: A delivery commits more than ten minutes behind the newest id seen, and the cursor has passed it.
gaps.question: The statement says a late commit is never lost, while the form's cursor bounds lateness at ten minutes. Is ten minutes the stated bound, or must a later commit still be found, and how?

gaps.failure_way: After erasure the kept row still holds the Message-ID in plain text, which toy 01a1a4ad found survives deletion in SQLite files.
gaps.question: Which fields may the row kept after erasure hold (blob key, a keyed hash of the Message-ID, size, internal date, flags), given that the form's messages table stores message_id as plain text?

gaps.failure_way: A second delivery reusing or guessing a held Message-ID is skipped as held-message-id, hiding different mail from the person.
gaps.question: Does a held-message-id skip of different mail count as a lost delivery under this requirement's title, or is it accepted as the receiving form's 'shown to the person once'?

gaps.failure_way: A tell arrives five minutes late, through the alarm, after a lost ping or tell.
gaps.question: How soon must a registered session be told of a change? The statement sets no bound, the alarm gives five minutes, and the form's event 3 expects Apple Mail to hear new mail within a minute.
